title: Call getTools() on a page that declares no tools
question: what does document.modelContext.getTools() return on a page that declares no tools — an empty list, a throw, or undefined?

answer.statement: On this instance and browser version, document.modelContext is an object whose prototype carries getTools (beside registerTool, executeTool, ontoolchange, ontoolactivated and ontoolcancel, which T001 recorded statically). getTools() does not return the list: it returns a Promise. Awaited on a page that declares no tools, that promise resolves to an empty array — the JSON of the resolved value is [], its constructor is Array and its length is 0. So the answer to the question this task was asked to measure is: neither an empty list returned synchronously, nor a throw, nor undefined — an asynchronously resolved empty list.

effectOnTheReader.judgement: Array.isArray on the getter’s synchronous return
effectOnTheReader.reasonDetail: the list getter answered an object rather than a list: the tool list is not readable
effectOnTheReader.statement: The reader calls the getter once, with no argument, and judges the value it returned with Array.isArray. A Promise is an object rather than a list, so the measured API answers the reader cannot-tell with code unreadable-list and the detail above — not empty, even though the promise resolves to []. The units agree on the fact and disagree on the shape: the page declared no tools and the API said so, but not through a value the reader can read synchronously. Whether readTools should await the getter is not this task’s to change (extension/webmcp-audit.js is T002’s file), and this recording states the observation rather than editing the reader.

notClaimed: Nothing here claims getTools() is synchronous on any other browser version or instance: one instance (chrome-beta-nano, Chrome/159.0.8154.13) and one page were measured, and research/raw/m052-webmcp-api.json’s unknowns[member-list-still-current] is why the version is recorded beside the result.

Nothing here claims a page that declares a tool lists it: the page measured declares none, so the only value observed is the empty resolution. A tool descriptor’s fields are T001’s documented shape and T002’s fixture, never an observation of this page.

Nothing here claims the panel reads a live page’s tool list: the panel renders the reading it is handed (apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-webmcp.ts), and no code in this tree relays getTools() from an inspected tab.

Nothing here re-measures the prototype member list beyond the names this run printed: the members recorded above are the ones this browser version answered with, which is a re-measurement of T001’s 2026-10-11 reading rather than a copy of it.
